hook: The most revealing thing about someone isn't how they treat you when they care about you — it's what they do the first time something doesn't go their way
topic: Stress behaviour as character data — how pressure reveals patterns
body:
**The most revealing thing about someone isn't how they treat you when everything is easy. It's what they do the first time something doesn't go their way.**

When things are good, almost everyone is their best self. Patient. Generous. Engaged. Easy to be around. None of that tells you who you're actually dealing with — because being pleasant when life is pleasant requires very little of a person.

What requires something is friction. A plan that changes. A boundary being set. A moment where they want something and can't have it. That's when you see the actual operating system.

Some people get quiet and withdraw. Some redirect blame faster than you can track it. Some escalate immediately, then act as though it didn't happen. Some become very, very nice in a way that feels subtly like pressure.

All of these are patterns. And they will repeat. The first time you see one isn't a bad day. It's a preview.

The people who end up consistently blindsiding us are rarely people who gave us nothing to go on. They're people whose patterns we saw early and explained away. "They were stressed." "It was a difficult situation." "That's not normally who they are."

It is who they are. The easy moments are the performance. The hard moments are the person.

Watch for the first small moment of difficulty with someone new. That's your most accurate data point.
